root_cause.text: In fs/smb/client/smbdirect.c, smbd_post_send_iter() incorrectly retained ownership of a send_io request after smbd_post_send() had moved it into the batch list, causing the same request to be freed again when smbd_send_batch_flush() had already freed it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the comment “From here request is moved to batch and we should not free it explicitly,” changes the error path after smbd_send_batch_flush() failure to jump to err_flush instead of err_dma, and the commit message explicitly states “smbd_send_batch_flush() already calls smbd_free_send_io(), so we should not call it again.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In fs/smb/client/smbdirect.c, smbd_post_send_iter() incorrectly retained ownership of a send_io request after smbd_post_send() had moved it into the batch list, causing the same request to be freed again when smbd_send_batch_flush() had already freed it.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds the comment “From here request is moved to batch and we should not free it explicitly,” changes the error path after smbd_send_batch_flush() failure to jump to err_flush instead of err_dma, and the commit message explicitly states “smbd_send_batch_flush() already calls smbd_free_send_io(), so we should not call it again.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid freeing a send request after ownership has transferred to the batch when batch flush fails, while still restoring credits on error.
intent_record.what: The change adds a comment clarifying that after a successful smbd_post_send(sc, batch, request) call the request ownership is transferred to the batch, inserts a goto err_flush after a failed smbd_send_batch_flush(sc, batch, true) when batch == &_batch, and introduces a new err_flush label placed after the smbd_free_send_io(request) path so that flush failures skip explicitly freeing the request while still executing the credit restoration logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if posting the send succeeds but flushing the local batch fails, execution now avoids calling smbd_free_send_io(request) on a request that has already been moved into the batch. This prevents an invalid or double free while still restoring send credits and waking waiters on the error path.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid freeing a send request after ownership has transferred to the batch when batch flush fails, while still restoring credits on error.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the ownership-transfer bug in smbd_post_send_iter(): it avoids freeing a send request after smbd_post_send() has moved it into the batch list, matching the root cause of the double free while preserving credit restoration on error.

candidates.rationale: This free occurs on the error path even after smbd_post_send() may already have transferred ownership of request into the batch list; if batch flush then already freed it, this causes a double free.

When this flush fails after smbd_post_send() has queued the request into the batch, the batch machinery may already have consumed/freed the request, making the subsequent unconditional free of request invalid.
This call is the ownership transfer point: after success, request may no longer be owned by the caller. The later error path incorrectly still treats request as caller-owned and frees it again.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional free on the error path is the direct double-free site. After smbd_post_send() transfers ownership of request into the batch, a failing smbd_send_batch_flush() may already have freed or consumed that request, so freeing it here again triggers the vulnerability.
This is the ownership transfer point for request. The later error path becomes invalid because it still assumes caller ownership after this call may have moved request into the batch list.
If this flush fails after the request has already been handed to the batch, batch handling may already have freed or otherwise consumed request, making the subsequent caller-side free invalid.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the full ownership/queueing logic for batching in `smbd_post_send()`, `smbd_send_batch_flush()`, and the caller `smbd_post_send_iter()`. The vulnerable construct is present: in `smbd_post_send()`, when `batch` is non-NULL, the function links `request` into `batch->msg_list` via `list_add_tail(&request->sibling_list, &batch->msg_list);`, increments `batch->wr_cnt`, and `return 0;`. That means ownership of `request` has been transferred into the batch. Later, `smbd_send_batch_flush()` removes the last request, splices the other queued requests into `last->sibling_list`, posts the chain, and on error explicitly frees all siblings plus `last` with `smbd_free_send_io(...)`. Also on completion, `send_done()` frees all siblings and then the main request. However, in `smbd_post_send_iter()`, after `rc = smbd_post_send(sc, batch, request);`, the code only does `if (!rc) return 0;` and otherwise falls into the existing error path. There is no indication that `request` is cleared/nullified or detached after a successful batched `smbd_post_send()`. Because success in batched mode means the request is merely queued into the batch, the caller still retaining its local `request` for later cleanup is exactly the root-cause pattern: ownership was moved, but the caller was not prevented from freeing it again. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present in this commit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full ownership/error-handling path inside `smbd_post_send_iter()` and the relevant interaction with `smbd_post_send()`/`smbd_send_batch_flush()`. The root cause to look for is: after `smbd_post_send(sc, batch, request)` succeeds and transfers ownership of `request` into the batch list, `smbd_post_send_iter()` must not later free the same `request`. In this commit, after `rc = smbd_post_send(sc, batch, request);`, the code does `if (!rc) { if (batch != &_batch) return 0; rc = smbd_send_batch_flush(sc, batch, true); if (!rc) return 0; }`. If `smbd_post_send()` succeeds, then either the function returns immediately for external batches, or flushes the local batch and returns on successful flush. However, if `smbd_post_send()` succeeds but `smbd_send_batch_flush(sc, batch, true)` fails, execution falls through to `err_dma:` which unconditionally calls `smbd_free_send_io(request);`. At that point, ownership had already been moved into the batch by successful `smbd_post_send()`, so this preserves the vulnerable double-free pattern described in the root cause. Therefore the vulnerable construct is still present. As for the fix, the commit adds batch credits (`wait_for_send_bcredit()`, `batch->credit`, releasing credit in `smbd_send_batch_flush()`), but it does not add logic to clear `request` ownership after successful `smbd_post_send()` or otherwise prevent `err_dma:` from freeing an already-batched request. So the specific fix for the double-free is not present.
